answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before it earns rewards, like a cedar planted with deep roots: cheap to sprout, costly to uproot. Peers then attest to real work, and a lantern of transparent reputation follows every account, so a fresh copy cannot borrow the trust of an established one. If an identity cheats, its stake is slashed and its mirror record — the public history of its actions — stays stained, making each new fake identity pay the full price again.
